title: Highlights
content: NEWS HIGHLIGHTS Science Breaking Boundaries Team Science for National Security For more than 70 years, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has made seemingly impossible innovations a reality through the combination of preeminent science, technology and engineering. Our "team science" approach to problem solving brings together dynamic individuals from many different disciplines to work on big, galvanizing challenges. While our enduring mission of enabling U.S. security and global stability and resilience largely focuses on nuclear deterrence, that work formed the foundation for myriad breakthroughs including fusion ignition, supercomputing-aided drug design and sophisticated earth systems modeling. “At LLNL, we apply world-leading science and technology to address today’s most significant national security challenges, ranging from critical issues in nuclear deterrence to important questions in energy security.” – Kim Budil DIRECTOR, LAWRENCE LIVERMORE NATIONAL LABORATORY From creating self-driving labs and digital twins that streamline production workflows to accelerated drug discovery, LLNL researchers are using AI to meet some of the nation's toughest national security needs. AI at LLNL Artificial intelligence (AI) is a critical part of LLNL's national security work. Our researchers use AI to advance strategic deterrence, stockpile modernization, materials discovery, fusion research, advanced manufacturing and energy resilience, helping to build AI-enabled capabilities that streamline and enhance mission delivery. Learn More About LLNL's Ongoing AI Efforts See Our Work in Action Watch: Harnessing the power of AI for a safe and secure future Watch: How LLNL helped build the world's largest camera Watch: LLNL 2025 highlights LLNL Goes Exascale Computing at LLNL took a leap forward with the addition the of El Capitan supercomputer. Capable of more than two quintillion (10 18 ) calculations per second, El Capitan's unprecedented processing power enables stockpile management and cements the U.S.'s leadership in complex, high-fidelity modeling and simulation. Learn More About El Capitan El Capitan, the National Nuclear Security Administration's first exascale computer, is projected to bring more than two exaFLOPs of processing power to LLNL's efforts to ensure that the U.S. nuclear stockpile is safe, secure and reliable. LLNL Achieves Fusion Ignition On Dec. 5, 2022, an LLNL experiment ushered in “The Age of Ignition” with an experiment that produced more energy from a fusion reaction than the energy needed to spark the reaction, a condition known as ignition. Decades in the making, this accomplishment supports our national security mission and demonstrated the scientific basis for inertial fusion energy.
